- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) or shows sharp decline, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off or volatility squeeze.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (especially >72.5) by forecasting further upward; cap or dampen forecast after spike.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0–0.5), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply mild downward bias toward historical mean of last 7–14 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: model tends to be 1–2 days behind true trend; adjust by adding 0.5–1.0 point lag correction if sentiment is trending.
- When sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.8 → 0.0 → 0.27), model overfits recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3–5% gap), sentiment may be overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period unless sentiment shifts.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome and sentiment is weak or negative, model may be ignoring macro risk; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
